title: Additional beginner modules (data/SQL basics, files, simple projects)
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). Once two language modules are solid, additional content widens the curriculum to cover practical next-steps topics: reading/writing files, basic data manipulation (SQL or pandas basics), and small complete projects that integrate concepts. These extend the curriculum's reach without changing its model.
objective: Author additional beginner modules covering practical next-steps topics — file I/O in Python, basic SQL or data manipulation, and at least one small complete project that integrates multiple lesson concepts — each following the same schema, correctness gate, and review process.
acceptanceCriteria: At least 3 lessons are delivered covering practical next-steps topics; the specific topic set is confirmed with the education partner before authoring.
Every lesson has at least 1 runnable example and at least 1 graded exercise with solutionVerified:true and starter code that does NOT pass the tests.
At least one lesson delivers a 'small complete project' that integrates ≥ 3 concepts from earlier lessons.
All prose is original; at least 2 authoritative cited sources per lesson.
Schema-valid; technical + pedagogy review by non-authors.
Partner confirms the chosen topic set is relevant to their learners before authoring begins.
output: A set of merged lesson documents for additional beginner topics (file I/O, data basics, and a complete project), each schema-valid, correctness-verified, and reviewed.
